title: Predictive Value of the Cincinnati Scale for Code Stroke Activation in Relation to CT Scan Findings
content: Background: Stroke is the second leading cause of death worldwide and main cause of disability in adults. Timely care is essential to achieve reperfusion and preserve brain tissue. Efforts have been made to correlate CT signs with the Cincinnati Prehospital Stroke Scale to activate the Comprehensive Stroke Protocol. Analyzing these factors may provide useful parameters for selection. Material and Methods: This analytical, cross-sectional, observational, prospective study was conducted at the Regional General Hospital in Orizaba, Mexico. A total of 497_20 non-contrast cranial CT scans were analyzed using PACS. Patients were followed through medical records until discharge diagnosis was confirmed. Data collection occurred from March 2024_45. Results: 497_2 CT scans were reviewed. The Stroke Code was most often used in the 70-79-year age group, with 56.9% female patients. Of 72_24 ischemic stroke cases, only 24_29 were within the therapeutic window. Conclusion: The Cincinnati scale as a rapid cerebrovascular screen has only moderate to low discriminatory ability. Sensitivity and positive predictive value are very low. Therefore, it is not suitable alone. The results provide opportunity to train doctors to use the Cincinnati scale alongside the NIHSS scale, which has better predictive ability. More public education is recommended to help patients present within the window.
